title: Stopping on the last success with unknown odds: asymptotic minimax optimality of the plug-in rule
summary: We study the last-success problem for sequential Bernoulli trials in the homogeneous setting where $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are i.i.d. $\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$ but the success probability $p\in(0,1)$ is unknown to the decision maker. When $p$ is known, Bruss' sum-the-odds theorem yields an optimal threshold rule with win probability $V_n(p)$; when it is not, the odds driving this threshold must be learned from the very sequence on which one is trying to stop, which turns the problem into a genuinely statistical decision problem over the class of $p$-blind rules---those depending on the data but not…
